pamphlets.title: Garrison Standing Order 102: Emergency Protocol
pamphlets.doctrine: Civil Defense Directive 9 takes precedence over township custom. Rations are fuel for the defense infrastructure. A dead soldier cannot hold the intake valve.
pamphlets.liturgy: The perimeter is the wall; the wall is the life; outside the wall is the dust.

pamphlets.doctrine: The soil does not recognize military command. What is planted in poisoned dirt yields only poisoned bread. Seed wheat must be protected before human wounded.
pamphlets.liturgy: Two inches of clean compost stands between the province and cannibalism.

pamphlets.doctrine: Price is the only honest language left in a ruined world. Subsidies breed lazy stokers; charity creates beggars with knives. Calibrated scales prevent war.
pamphlets.liturgy: Weigh the silver, weigh the salt, weigh the soul; all three have a price.

pamphlets.doctrine: The low marsh belongs to those who maintain the sumps. Clean distillate has a production cost in coal and zinc filters. Pay the tariff or drink the runoff.
pamphlets.liturgy: Water is blood; the pump is the heart; the tariff is the breath.

pamphlets.doctrine: The ash outside is our penance. In the dark kiln, wood becomes black carbon that scrubs the air of poison. We burn what was green to protect what is buried.
pamphlets.liturgy: From wood to coal, from coal to smoke, from smoke to clean breath.

pamphlets.doctrine: The drowned canals are our streets. The rowers take the risk in the acid squalls; the rowers take the first salvage. No officer commands the oar.
pamphlets.liturgy: Pull together or drown together; the brine takes no excuses.

pamphlets.doctrine: If the children forget the names of the pre-war cities and the principles of geometry, the survival of this bunker is merely the survival of beasts.
pamphlets.liturgy: The slate is our weapon; the chalk is our light.

pamphlets.doctrine: The automated apparatus does not sleep, weep, or negotiate. 211,004 were registered; all discrepancies must be reconciled on the ledger.
pamphlets.liturgy: Count, record, balance. The machine endures.

pamphlets.doctrine: The hardest math is knowing which four hundred people must drown so that four thousand can eat next winter. A sapper does not ask for forgiveness.
pamphlets.liturgy: The fuse burns down; the concrete falls; the valley lives.

pamphlets.doctrine: Without our heat, the cold takes the valley in forty-eight hours. The furnace floor is the backbone of civilization. Treat the iron master with respect.
pamphlets.liturgy: Iron in the vein, coal in the lung, heat in the home.

pamphlets.doctrine: Look to the sky, not for rescue, but for falling iron. The constellations of the old world are decaying. When the sky falls, shield the ground.
pamphlets.liturgy: We watch the tracks; we track the dead; we ring the bell.

pamphlets.doctrine: Every person who died in the cellar deserves their name carved in stone. A society that forgets the names of its dead loses its claim to the future.
pamphlets.liturgy: Chisel deep, cut true; granite does not lie.

pamphlets.doctrine: Triage is the only law. We give the medicine to the worker who turns the pump, not the elder who sits in the cot. Cold compassion saves lives.
pamphlets.liturgy: Hold the key, measure the dose, close the book.

pamphlets.doctrine: The lock gates are the gates of the valley. Keep the silt dredged, the chains greased, and the contraband under armed watch.
pamphlets.liturgy: Clear the lock, hold the gate, guard the water.

pamphlets.doctrine: The war is ten years behind us. We are no longer survivors hiding in holes; we are the founding citizens of the Tessarat Commonwealth.
pamphlets.liturgy: From shelter to town, from fear to law, from ash to green.

pamphlets.doctrine: Travel light, walk by night, keep the dosimeter dry, and never speak the name of your home shelter to a stranger on the ice road.
pamphlets.liturgy: Follow the ridge, check the wind, keep moving.
